stories.headline: Will Anderson calls Texans’ loss to Bills a 'wake-up call' for the defense ahead of Bengals visit
stories.summary: — Houston Texans defensive end Will Anderson said giving up 36 points in a season-opening loss to the Bills wasn’t a reason to get mad but instead should be a catalyst to improve.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- — Houston Texans defensive end Will Anderson said giving up 36 points in a season-opening loss to the Bills wasn’t a reason to get mad but instead should be a catalyst to improve.


“That’s probably the best thing that could have happened to us,” he said. “We got hit in the mouth and now we know how to respond. Now it’s a wake-up call for everybody.”


The Texans look to bounce back from that uncharacteristically poor performance when they host the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. They’re coming off a 33-27 win over Tampa Bay in their opener.


And they know better than to underestimate Houston’s defense, which was among the league’s best last season, despite the lackluster performance on opening weekend.


“They are very fast, very physical,” Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. “Not only are they very talented and well-coached but they play really good together as a unit… (we've) certainly got our work cut out for us. They have elite talent across the board on their defense and it poses a lot of challenges for you.”


Quarterback Joe Burrow was limited in practice Wednesday as he deals with back tightness and “normal game day soreness.” But the three-time Pro Bowler said there’s no way the problem would keep him out against the Texans.


“That’s ridiculous,” Burrow said.


After dealing with Josh Allen last week, the Texans know their defense will have its hands full again in trying to slow down Burrow and the Cincinnati offense. He threw for 254 yards with a touchdown and interception against the Buccaneers.


“The Bengals are a really exceptional offense,” Houston coach DeMeco Ryans said. “Everything starts and goes through the quarterback. Talk about a guy that has exceptional talent, Joe Burrow, he’s one of the best quarterbacks I’ve watched and studied.”


While Houston certainly respects Burrow and his talented offense, Anderson said the key to success this week will be for the Texans to focus on themselves.


“The biggest thing is just going out there and having fun,” he said. “Not overcomplicating football. Not getting too high. Not getting too low. But just playing our brand of ball and having fun doing that.”


Need to know
Cincinnati (1-0) at Houston (0-1)


When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, CBS.


Latest odds: Texans by 2½.


Against the spread: Bengals 1-0; Texans 0-1.


Last week: Bengals beat Buccaneers 33-27; Texans lost to Bills 36-31.


Last meeting: Texans beat Bengals 30-27 on Nov. 12, 2023, in Cincinnati.


Series record: Texans lead 9-5.


Matchup to watch
Cincinnati WRs Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins vs Houston’s secondary. The Texans allowed Allen to throw for 334 yards last week and they’ll be challenged again by Cincinnati’s star-studded offense.


The unit gave up multiple explosive plays against the Bills, including touchdown receptions of 43 and 34 yards.


Higgins had 59 yards receiving last week but Chase, who had 1,412 yards receiving last season, had just two catches for 12 yards. Burrow knows that has to change this week.


“We’ve got to get him involved,” Burrow said. “That sentiment was echoed from a lot of different fronts after the game and can’t come out of a game like that and have Ja’Marr Chase touch the ball two times. So that certainly will be an emphasis.”


Stats and stuff
— Burrow tied for the league lead in quick completions last week with 20 (throws in under 2.5 seconds). Anderson has 93 QB pressures since the start of last season — second most in the league — with 40 happening in under 2.5 seconds.


— Houston QB C.J. Stroud completed passes to 11 different receivers Sunday.


— Chase needs seven catches to pass former Texans star DeAndre Hopkins (528) for the fourth-most receptions by a player in his first six seasons in NFL history. He had five receptions for 124 yards and a touchdown in his most recent meeting with Houston.


— Houston WR Nico Collins had 75 yards receiving and a touchdown last week to give him at least 50 yards receiving in 10 consecutive regular-season games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL.


— The Bengals lead the NFL in takeaways after recovering four fumbles last week.


— RB David Montgomery had two rushing touchdowns and a scoring reception in the opener to become the first Texan to score three touchdowns in his debut after an offseason trade from Detroit. He had 65 yards rushing an a touchdown in his most recent game against the Bengals last season.


— Cincinnati LB Demetrius Knight Jr. had seven tackles and his first career fumble return for a touchdown on a 27-yard score in the first quarter in Week 1.

Pitchers to stream Friday

Given that winning and losing streaks can flip at any time, Ian Seymour and the Tampa Bay Rays are catching the Boston Red Sox at the right time, with the visitors struggling in September, especially facing left-handed pitching. The Rays have clinched a playoff berth, but until they secure the AL East and the No. 1 seed in the American League, they'll play their regulars. Barring a collapse, the Red Sox appear locked into the second AL wild-card spot. Ceddanne Rafaela remains sidelined for the Red Sox, aiding Seymour.
The Chicago Cubs visit the Cincinnati Reds in an NL Central matchup. Clay Holmes takes the hill for the visitors and faces a lineup with the second-lowest wOBA and highest strikeout rate against righties for the season. Recently, the Reds have been even worse, sporting a lower wOBA and higher strikeout rate.
Dustin May was initially set to start Thursday's series finale with the Pittsburgh Pirates, but the Milwaukee Brewers opted to give Kyle Harrison the nod in Steel City. Instead, May draws the Baltimore Orioles in Camden Yards. He'll pitch in a better hitter's park, but the Orioles have been far less productive than the Pirates facing right-handers. May is trying to earn a spot in the Brewers' playoff rotation and is coming off a solid effort where he tossed six scoreless innings against the Reds, fanning six with just one walk.

Hitters to stream on Thursday

Seattle Mariners hitters are enjoying a huge park upgrade, leaving T-Mobile Park for a weekend set against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Dominic Canzone and J.P. Crawford reap a further benefit, holding the platoon edge on Ryan Feltner and his 5.71 home ERA.
Randal Grichuk is batting a robust .389/.410/.694 in September. The veteran right-handed hitter will be in the Chicago White Sox lineup when they take on the Detroit Tigers and lefty Andrew Sears at home.
Henry Bolte is quietly putting up a solid final two months. Since July 31, he's hitting .311/.395/.503 with eight homers and eight steals over 43 games. The Athletics are on the road to play the Cleveland Guardians. The righty swinger will lead off the game against right-handed opener Daniel Espino, but then he should see lefty bulk reliever Joey Cantillo a couple of times.
Teoscar Hernandez has accrued ample career plate appearances for his success facing left-handers to be statistically significant. The Los Angeles Dodgers host the San Francisco Giants and rookie southpaw Cesar Perdomo.
Paul Goldschmidt is another example of a veteran right-handed batter with meaningfully elevated splits against left-handers. The New York Yankees are in the desert with southpaw Eduardo Rodriguez getting the call for the Arizona Diamondbacks.

stories.headline: Weekend predictions: Madrid derby heats up LaLiga, Brighton to stun Arsenal?
stories.summary: It's another big weekend of matches in Europe which will include heated derbies, top-of-the-table matchups and other rivalries.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 club season is just a month old, and we are already heading into an international break, but as the European fixture list proves, there are some heavyweight clashes this weekend before the three-week -- yes, three-week -- international break kicks in.

There are some classic derbies, top-of-the-table matches and long-standing rivalries ready for a new chapter across the continent over the coming days. And this weekend, get ready for stand-out games in Italy, Spain, England, Portugal, Scotland, France and renewal of hostilities in the East End of London.

- Connelly: World soccer's hottest men's teams right now

- Ogden: Soccer should learn from the NFL to fix VAR mess

- O'Hanlon: Which Premier League managers will be fired first?

Top two in Italy square up in heavyweight clash

AS Roma vs. Internazionale

Serie A, Matchday 5

Kickoff: Saturday, 12:00 p.m. ET / 5:00 p.m. BST

This is the game of the weekend in all of Europe, as it pits the early pacesetters in Italy against each other in a fixture where something has to give between two sides defending 100% winning records in Serie A.

Roma, chasing their first Scudetto since 2001, face reigning champions Inter at the Stadio Olimpico as league leaders due to their superior goal difference. Gian Piero Gasperini's team have scored 12 and conceded just one goal in four games so far, with Netherlands forward Donyell Malen hitting six goals already for the Giallorossi and Paulo Dybala registering four assists.

But Inter, who have won two of the last three Serie A title races, travel to Rome as the dominant force in Italy and will face Gasperini's team determined to strike a blow against their early challengers. Inter have won 10 and lost two of their last 12 meetings with Roma dating back to 2021, so Saturday's clash will be a real test of Roma's title credentials.

MY PREDICTION: Roma 2-1 Inter. Roma have made a formidable start to the season and their defense is stronger than Inter's, so that gives the home side the edge.

Madrid derby heats up title race

Atlético Madrid vs. Real Madrid

LaLiga, Matchday 7

Kickoff: Sunday, 10:15 a.m. ET / 3:15 p.m. BST

The 244th Madrid derby is all about which team emerges as the biggest challenger to reigning champions and unbeaten LaLiga leaders Barcelona.

Jose Mourinho's side head to the Metropolitano on Sunday three points behind Barça after a 1-0 defeat at Real Betis on Sept. 4 gave them an early loss on their record.

Atlético, two points further back in third, have made an inconsistent start to the season, with a home draw against Villarreal and a 3-0 defeat away to Athletic Club. But Diego Simeone's side has since bounced back by scoring seven goals and conceding none in wins against Real Sociedad and Osasuna, so they will face Real with confidence growing and the likelihood of Julián Álvarez being fit to play after a recent muscle injury.

Real start as favorites, with Kylian Mbappé already in form with seven goals in LaLiga so far, but Atleti's recent run gives them hope.

MY PREDICTION: Atleti 1-3 Real. Real are just stronger all round and even if Álvarez is fit to play, how fit is he really after so long off the training pitch?

Can the Seagulls stop the Gunners' unbeaten run?

Brighton & Hove Albion vs. Arsenal

Premier League, Matchday 5

Kickoff: Saturday, 10:00 a.m ET / 3:00 p.m. BST

There is already talk in England of Arsenal going unbeaten this season and matching the historic feat of Arsene Wenger's 2004 Invincibles, but is that usual early-season hyperbole, or a realistic outcome for Mikel Arteta's champions?

In truth, it's both. It's way too early to predict an unbeaten season, but Arsenal have looked so strong at the start of their title defense -- seven wins from seven games and just three goals conceded in all competitions -- that it's already difficult to pick out many slip-ups.

But their trip to face Brighton at the Amex is certainly a potential bump in the road for the Gunners. Fabian Hürzeler's Seagulls are the top scorers so far in the Premier League with 13 goals in four games, and they fought back from 2-0 in midweek to win 3-2 against Manchester United in the Carabao Cup.

Hürzeler is a rising star in coaching, and his spat with Arteta over Arsenal's tactics last season will add spice to this game.

MY PREDICTION: Brighton 0-2 Arsenal. Arsenal rested key players in their Carabao Cup win at Ipswich Town on Tuesday, but Hürzeler went strong at Old Trafford 24 hours later, so fatigue is likely to be significant for the home side.

A Rosenior homecoming

Paris FC vs. Strasbourg

Ligue 1, Matchday 5

Kickoff: Saturday, 11:15 a.m. ET / 4:15 p.m. BST

There are big derby games all over Europe this weekend, so how about the Liam Rosenior derby between Paris FC and Strasbourg at Stade Jean-Bouin?

This time last year, Rosenior was quietly making a name for himself as Strasbourg coach, managing several on-loan Chelsea players -- Strasbourg and Chelsea are owned by parent company BlueCo -- while establishing Les Bleu et Blanc at the top end of Ligue 1.

We all know what happened next. Chelsea fired Enzo Maresca as coach in January and moved Rosenior from Strasbourg to Stamford Bridge in what proved to be a dismal 23-game spell in charge for the 42-year-old.

But Rosenior is now rebuilding his reputation with Paris FC, guiding the club to fourth in Ligue 1 after an unbeaten start to the season and they face sixth-place Strasbourg knowing that a win could take them top if second-place AS Monaco fail to beat Lens on Friday.

MY PREDICTION: Paris FC 2-0 Strasbourg. Strasbourg have the leakiest defense in the top half and Paris have the momentum, so this is a home win.

Showdown between Portuguese giants

FC Porto vs. Benfica

Portuguese Primeira Liga, Matchday 7

Kickoff: Friday, 3:30 p.m. ET / 8:30 p.m. BST

Five teams are still unbeaten in the Portuguese league after six games so far this season, but top two sides Porto and Benfica are already pulling away from the chasing pack.

Defending champions Porto have won all six of their league games so far and Francesco Farioli's side haven't lost a league game at Estádio do Dragão since Apr. 2025. But that defeat -- a 4-1 loss -- was given by Benfica in a game that saw Vangelis Pavlidis score a hat trick.

So with former Fulham coach Marco Silva now in charge of the Lisbon giants, who have won five and drawn one of their six games so far, Porto's long home streak will face a stern test on Sunday. Greece international Pavlidis is already leading the Golden Boot race with eight goals this season, so Benfica will fancy their chances of a win this weekend.

MY PREDICTION: Porto 2-2 Benfica. This is a real heavyweight clash in Porto, and both sides are in form, so it will be tough for either team to get the win.

Old Firm becomes first big early test

Celtic vs. Rangers

Scottish Premiership, Matchday 4

Kickoff: Sunday, 7:00 a.m. ET / 12:00 p.m. BST

Here we go again: the sport's most deep-seated rivalry and the one with the longest history. Celtic and Rangers have faced each other 453 times and the head-to-head is incredibly close, with Rangers claiming 173 wins and Celtic 172.

Martin O'Neill's Celtic are already five points clear of their Old Firm rivals having won six from six in the league so far -- Rangers have lost one and drawn one -- but a 3-0 League Cup win at Ibrox last Sunday has given Rangers momentum going into their trip to Celtic Park. Derek McInnes, hired as coach from Hearts this summer, has had a turbulent start as Rangers boss, but beating Celtic last week has transformed his standing among the supporters and another positive result this weekend will banish any remaining negativity.

Due to crowd trouble during recent games, no away fans will be allowed at Celtic-Rangers games this season, so home advantage will be huge on each occasion.

MY PREDICTION: Celtic 3-1 Rangers. Rangers are improving under McInnes, but Celtic are formidable at home and that will shade it for the Bhoys this weekend.

Heated affair 14 years later

Millwall vs. West Ham United

English League Championship, Matchday 1

Kickoff: Saturday, 7:30 a.m. ET / 12:30 p.m. BST

Whenever there is a fan survey of the biggest rivalries in England, Millwall vs. West Ham -- the Dockers Derby -- often comes out on top, despite the two clubs from the East End of London rarely facing each other in recent times.

It is a rivalry rooted in union disputes dating back to the 1900s at long-since-closed dockyards, but the enmity between supporters has not faded.

Saturday's clash at The Den will be the 100th meeting between the two rivals and the first since Feb. 2012, and West Ham, top of the table following relegation from the Premier League last season, will be favorites to win. But Alex Neil's Millwall reached the Championship playoffs last season and their last home defeat against the Hammers was back in 1988, so local pride and the organization of the home side make this game much closer than league positions might suggest.

MY PREDICTION: Millwall 1-3 West Ham. This will be a heated derby, but West Ham still have stacks of Premier League quality and that will make the difference.

stories.headline: Defensive stalwart Watson ready to flex his versatility with Cavs
stories.summary: The Cavaliers weren't one of the first teams interested in acquiring Peyton Watson, but once they began their pursuit of the restricted free agent, the 23-year-old forward saw how it made sense for both parties.
stories.body:
INDEPENDENCE, Ohio -- The Cleveland Cavaliers weren't one of the first teams interested in acquiring Peyton Watson. However, once they began their pursuit of the restricted free agent, the 23-year-old forward saw how it made sense for both parties.

"They weren't one of the first teams that was speculated to be interested or one of the first teams that kind of came into the fold, but as soon as they were, they were interested," Watson said during a news conference Thursday at the Cavaliers' training complex.

Watson was acquired in a sign-and-trade that was part of a five-team deal in late August. He started a career-high 40 games last season with the Denver Nuggets and averaged career bests in points (14.6), rebounds (4.9) and assists (2.1).

Watson did admit it was hard to have patience during the summer because he was eager to resolve where he was going to play this season. The market was also in flux until late July when LeBron James signed with Philadelphia.

Once James decided he wouldn't return to Cleveland for a third stint, the Cavaliers stepped up their pursuit of Watson and eventually signed him to a four-year, $88 million contract.

The Cavaliers are hoping that Watson has the same type of impact that New York swingman OG Anunoby and Minnesota's Jaden McDaniels had with their teams. Cleveland made the Eastern Conference finals for the first time since 2018 last season before being swept by the Knicks in four games.

"We're really excited about what he's going to bring to the table right away, but I think even more than that, his best basketball is ahead of him. He's going to help us win some games, but I'm also really excited about his trajectory with us," president of basketball operations Koby Altman said before handing Watson a jersey with his name and No. 8 on the back.

Watson joins a starting lineup that has Evan Mobley at the other forward, Jarrett Allen at center and James Harden and Donovan Mitchell in the backcourt. Watson thinks being in a lineup with Mobley and Allen, who are very good at attacking the rim, can improve his defense.

"I feel like it just gives me a lot more leeway and a lot more rope to be more aggressive defensively. I think playing the passing lanes more aggressively and really push up on guys more knowing that I have that back line behind me and I have elite rim protection in JA and Evan," he said. "I think it makes our team a threat defensively because we can play very aggressive and very physical while at the same time not giving up too many shots at the rim."

Watson made 41.1% of his 3-pointers last season, but thinks he can be a bigger threat beyond the perimeter. He also understood why some have referred to him as a "3-and-D specialist" -- great long-distance shooters who are elite defenders -- but is hoping to show that he can be much more.

"I don't define myself by that term. I think that it doesn't encompass enough about me just as a person and as a player. I think that I strive to be somebody who can do a lot of different things well. But obviously coming into the league, that's an archetype that I wanted to fit into to get myself on the floor," he said. "I have to continue to grow and get better that I never like to box myself in one category."

stories.headline: Messi, MLS' Garber appear to have heated exchange after Miami win
stories.summary: Lionel Messi pointed his finger at MLS commissioner Don Garber on multiple occasions while speaking with him after Inter Miami's game with Cruz Azul on Wednesday.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi pointed his finger at MLS commissioner Don Garber on multiple occasions while speaking with him after Inter Miami's game with Cruz Azul on Wednesday.

Postgame video showed Messi pointing at Garber and speaking to him before walking away. He then appears later in the video pointing at him and talking to him again. Another video showed them pointing at each other as they spoke.

MLS declined comment on the matter. Inter Miami didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The exchange came after Inter Miami defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 to win the Campeones Cup. Messi scored the 100th goal of his Inter Miami career during the game.

This victory gave Inter Miami another trophy three years after Messi's arrival. Miami won the Leagues Cup in 2023, the Supporters' Shield in 2024 and MLS Cup in 2025.

stories.headline: UFC 331 preview and picks: Pantoja sees opportunity in disaster
stories.summary: Top storylines and coaches' analysis for UFC 331 in Los Angeles.
stories.body:
For two and a half years, Alexandre Pantoja ruled the UFC's flyweight division at a level unseen since the historic era of Demetrious Johnson nearly 10 years ago. And yet, the past nine months since his last fight could prove to be the most compelling of Pantoja's career.
The 36-year-old Pantoja (30-6) will challenge Joshua Van (17-2) for the 125-pound championship at UFC 331 inside Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Saturday. It will be his first appearance since UFC 323 in December, when he lost the belt to Van via TKO after Pantoja suffered a dislocated elbow 26 seconds into the fight. The nature of the loss has led to a feeling of unfinished business between the two fighters going into Saturday's main event.

"As an athlete, yes, I have a TKO loss on my record," Pantoja told ESPN. "I've never lost by TKO or submission before. Nobody had ever finished me. Now, I have that. But personally, as a man? No. I don't believe I have a loss to him."

Pantoja won the title against Brandon Moreno in 2023 and defended the belt four times before meeting Van. He was among the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world at the time. But with a comeback narrative attached to him for this fight, he said there is an added level of excitement.

"For sure, this is an opportunity," Pantoja said. "In my soul, that's the opportunity. Now, I get to fight the champion. He's the champion of the world and I love that. It makes the fight more spicy for me."

Van, 24, has embraced the narrative -- even while cementing himself as the undisputed champion. There are those who say Van needs to defeat Pantoja again to legitimize his championship, but Van's first title defense against Tatsuro Taira in May made discrediting him harder. Taira's ground game posed a real threat to Van, but he ultimately knocked out the Japanese challenger in the fifth round of a matchup that earned fight of the night honors at UFC 328.

The unfinished business, Pantoja's return and Van's undeniable star power mean Saturday's flyweight title fight is shaping up to be the most anticipated 125-pound title fight since Henry Cejudo ended Johnson's nearly five-year title reign in 2018 then defended the flyweight belt against then-bantamweight champion TJ Dillashaw in 2019.

For Pantoja specifically, his worst stroke of bad luck could turn into the greatest night of his career.

"Saturday night is going to be my best night, man," Pantoja said. "I haven't been to work in 10 months. That's why all of these fights, and this one especially, is worth so much. We work for months to just get one night of work. I've recovered my arm. Now I have an opportunity to show everyone what I did in the last 10 months."

More storylines to watch
History isn't in Pantoja's favor
If Alexandre Pantoja is searching for role models to inspire this weekend's quest to reclaim the championship he lost suddenly and painfully last December, he would be wise to look beyond recent history.

Within the past two weeks, two of the UFC's 11 champs -- women's flyweight Valentina Shevchenko and heavyweight Tom Aspinall -- vacated their titles because of health issues. Their paths back to the top of the mountain are as yet uncharted.

Before them, the most recent champions to lose their titles to injuries did not fare well upon their returns. In November 2022, Jiří Procházka vacated the UFC light heavyweight title after hurting his shoulder in training. His successor was Jamahal Hill, who just months after winning the vacant title had to vacate it himself after rupturing an Achilles. As soon as he was healed, Hill was granted an opportunity to reclaim his title and lost. Procházka was given three shots at the 205-pound belt and fell short in all of them.

For a success story, Pantoja must look deeper into UFC championship history to the brutal health issues overcome by Dominick Cruz. While preparing for a bantamweight title defense in May 2012, Cruz tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee. He underwent surgery, then had a setback requiring a second ACL surgery six months later. He was scheduled to return in February 2014 but suffered a groin tear in training. Facing another extended recovery, he vacated his title.

Cruz returned that September and won a fight that put him in position for a shot at his old belt. Three months later, he tore his other ACL.

Finally, in February 2016 -- more than four years after his last title fight -- Cruz challenged TJ Dillashaw for the belt and won a split decision. "I had to show something to myself," Cruz said afterward. "That's what this was."

Tsarukyan's chance to set things right again
Arman Tsarukyan was labeled a snubbed man after it was announced that Justin Gaethje and Paddy Pimblett would headline the first UFC card of 2026 with the No. 1 lightweight contender status at stake. It's hard to remember that sentiment now, considering the year Tsarukyan has had.

In the absence of an obvious UFC fight to take, Tsarukyan has wrestled competitively -- mostly in RAF -- 10 times in 2026. He raised his social media presence exponentially behind videos of lavish cars, extraordinary meals and collaborations with content creator Nina Drama. This is the longest layoff of his UFC career, but his brand has grown more during that time off than from any single fight.

He appears in a good position to get back to work and finally earn the title shot many have said he should have already had. But it won't be an easy fight. Tsarukyan's opponent, Mauricio Ruffy, is a dangerous underdog (+270, according to DraftKings). This fight will restore the order the top of the 155-pound division has lacked in Tsarukyan's absence, regardless of who wins.

Another step for Steveson?

Any MMA prospect would almost certainly switch places with 26-year-old UFC newcomer Gable Steveson. When you're an Olympic gold medal wrestler, and one of the most touted heavyweight prospects in MMA history, certain opportunities are going to come to you that others aren't afforded. It also means Steveson's window for error is small, as he's asked to learn and develop under the sport's brightest lights.

The UFC is managing his opposition. For his second UFC appearance (and fifth pro fight overall), he'll take on Sean Sharaf, a 33-year-old with two knockout losses in his first two UFC fights. Steveson will once again be a heavy, heavy favorite (-2100 by DraftKings), as he was for his promotional debut in July. The heavyweight division is wide open now that Tom Aspinall has vacated his title and the list of top contenders is thin, so Steveson's performance probably means more than the result. If he continues to look the part, his career trajectory could be accelerated at a rate few see.

Coaches' questions and predictions
"Can Pantoja bank enough rounds on the ground, while staying responsible on the feet?"

What a fight this will be. Van shows up in big moments; he's just a proven gamer. If Pantoja stands with Van, he's going to get hurt. Pantoja is good at applying pressure and landing the 1-2 punch (lead left jab, right cross), but he cannot play that game with Van, because of Van's counterboxing. Van's hands are too fast. Van can land four-to-six shots at a time in close distance, and that's something Pantoja really has to watch for. Van is going to have confidence in his ability to get off the ground from his last fight against Taira. I'm going to stay on the fence and say it's a pick 'em. After watching Van's fight with Taira, though, knowing how good Taira is on the ground, it's a little unfair to say Van can't weather the storm on the ground with Pantoja. -- Sayif Saud, Fortis MMA

Prediction: Too close to call

"How big of a setback is Pantoja's injury at age 36?"
Van is young, fired up and he's got bricks in his hands. We've seen some small weaknesses in his game, which are obviously due to lack of experience. He's getting better all the time. If Pantoja comes back and is anywhere close to where he was when he was holding the belt, I think he gets it back. There are just too many variables on the ground. We saw Van get mounted by Taira. Van is going to go to work on fixing that hole in his game, but Pantoja is so good. The biggest question is how bad of a setback is Pantoja's injury, at this stage of his career? He's not a spring chicken. But if he's the same Pantoja, he gets the win, potentially by submission. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Prediction: Pantoja by decision or submission

"Can Ruffy stop takedowns and keep space?"

Arman has been on such a tear with the wrestling in RAF, showing his ability to wrestle bigger guys and show his power and skill in grappling. When it comes to that, he is very dangerous. Ruffy is finding his groove, and he's very sharp on the feet, but former opponents King Green and Michael Chandler don't pose the same grappling threat that Arman poses. I think Benoît Saint Denis kind of exposed that hole in Ruffy's game. It's not to say Ruffy doesn't have a chance. In space, he is a problem. He can absolutely starch Arman in space. But how does he keep a powerhouse like Arman at distance? -- Saud

Prediction: Tsarukyan by decision

"Has Ruffy improved his ground defense enough?"
This is a really interesting fight. Arman is going to want to grind out Ruffy. Arman is easily a top-five wrestler/grappler in the UFC. The one thing about Arman -- even though he's stayed busy with the wrestling appearances, he's been out of the UFC for a while, so it'll be interesting to see how he looks. But unless Ruffy catches him and knocks him out, Arman is a good striker, too. Arman can go the distance in a hard fight. My gut leans to Arman. I'm a big fan of Ruffy, but it's just that grappling prowess of Arman. -- Wood

Prediction: Tsarukyan by decision

ESPN's Jeff Wagenheim contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton shuts down asking Ferrari to make changes: 'Never asked for anyone to be replaced'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eight world championship is over.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eighth world championship is over.

Hamilton threw in the title towel at last weekend's Spanish Grand Prix after he retired from the race in Madrid with a brake problem.

His failure to finish leaves him 101 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the championship standings -- the equivalent of more than four victories -- with just nine scheduled rounds left.

A report in Italy claimed Hamilton has challenged Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur to make changes to the team's trackside staff.

But in a story posted to his Instagram account on Thursday, the 41-year-old wrote: "I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up on here.

"I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced. Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward.

"I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves.

"I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

- Lando Norris backs 'exciting' 2027 Monaco GP sprint weekend but 'tougher for us drivers'

- Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Hamilton sparked hope of challenging Antonelli -- the driver who replaced him at Mercedes -- when he won in Barcelona in June.

However, the British driver has not finished on the podium at the past five rounds and has been openly critical of his team's race tactics.

He also took aim at teammate Charles Leclerc's driving after an opening-lap clash in Monza earlier this month. Hamilton said he led face-to-face talks with the Monegasque to clear the air.

His retirement in Madrid marked his first of the campaign, and when asked to assess his title chances, Hamilton replied: "There's no stopping him [Antonelli] and Mercedes this year. They've done a phenomenal job, and they deserve it [the championship]."

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Bulldogs move to lock away rising rookie
stories.summary: Ronaldo Mulitalo is determined to honour his departing Sharks teammates, Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Bulldogs move early to lock down rising forward

The Bulldogs have moved early to lock down rising forward Alekolasimi 'AJ' Jones, with the club's Rookie of the Year agreeing to a two-year contract extension.

ESPN understands Jones, who was already contracted through the 2027 season, has agreed to a new deal that will keep him at Belmore beyond his existing contract.

The move ensures Jones' future is secured before he would have been free to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 from November 1.

Kennedy backs Hynes amid criticism

Will Kennedy believes Nicho Hynes has grown from the criticism that has followed him throughout his career, praising the Sharks star ahead of their semi-final against the Roosters.

"He's learned a lot from all the criticism he gets and he's taken a step forward," Kennedy said. "For me, I just want to get around him because he's my brother and I want to play next to him."

Trindall 'really good' after shoulder scare

Will Kennedy says Braydon Trindall has pulled up well after battling through a shoulder issue in Cronulla's finals win over North Queensland.

Kennedy said Trindall had been "really dialled in on the mental side" of his game and indicated the halfback had told him he was feeling "really good" ahead of the Roosters clash.

Mulitalo relishing 'Marky Mark' rematch

Ronaldo Mulitalo is embracing another blockbuster battle with Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase, describing the departing winger as a "generational talent".

Mulitalo said Nawaqanitawase "brings the best out of me" and revealed their on-field rivalry is largely one-sided when it comes to the verbal exchanges.

"He's a gentleman out there... he doesn't really say anything. I think it's more myself," Mulitalo joked. "He knows I'm just going to keep talking, so he just ignores me anyway."

Mulitalo determined to honour departing Sharks

Ronaldo Mulitalo says Cronulla's finals run carries added significance with several longtime teammates set to leave the club at season's end.

Mulitalo said he has played alongside some of the departing Sharks since he was 16 and wants to "honour those boys" with his performance against the Roosters.

"I don't want to let them down and disappoint them, winning the game is the most important part of the week for me."

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell
He also admitted the reality that every game could be his last for Cronulla is beginning to sink in.

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Cleary racing clock for preliminary final

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.headline: Falcons are looking for better defensive plan against Panthers QB Bryce Young in NFC South showdown
stories.summary: — The NFC South suffered the indignity of having four teams finish with losing...
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- — The NFC South suffered the indignity of having four teams finish with losing records last season and take Week 1 losses to open the 2026 season.


Last week's poor showing makes division matchups, including Carolina's visit to Atlanta on Sunday, especially important.


Though the Panthers finished with the same 8-9 regular-season record as Atlanta and Tampa Bay last season, they swept the two games against the Falcons on their way to winning the division title tiebreaker.


Panthers quarterback Bryce Young says coach Dave Canales has stressed that the best route to the playoffs is winning in the division.


“Coach talks about it all of the time," Young said. ”Our first goal is to win the South. Obviously those division wins mean so much when you’re trying to accomplish that goal. You have the same process for every game — you don’t get too high or too low, but this is a business and we are all players and we understand what is at stake every time there is a division opponent. We know what this game means.”


Atlanta's home opener follows a 20-13 opening loss at Pittsburgh last week. The Falcons were forced to start third-string quarterback Cooper Rush after Tua Tagovailoa suffered an oblique injury in practice and Michael Penix Jr. continued his recovery from a 2025 season-ending left knee injury.


Rush threw two interceptions, including T.J. Watt’s pick-6 in the fourth quarter.


Despite continued uncertainty at quarterback this week, the Falcons' bigger problem may be finding a way to contain Young and the Panthers' passing game. Young set a franchise record by passing for 448 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in Carolina's 30-27 overtime win at Atlanta to sweep the Falcons last season.


“He’s a very smart quarterback,” said Falcons safety Jessie Bates III of Young. "I think they’ve done a lot of really good things to help him bring out his strengths in his game, whether that’s them going to empty or rhythm-type of throws to help them out. I think that he’s definitely become a really high-level quarterback in this league for sure.”


Young's top playmakers are Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, an undrafted rookie in 2024 who had eight catches for a career-high 138 yards and two touchdowns in last week's 59-37 loss to Chicago.

Matchup to watch
Panthers run defense vs. Falcons running back Bijan Robinson. The Panthers allowed two Chicago running backs to reach 100 rushing yards in the Bears' 59-37 win last week in Charlotte. Overall, the Bears rushed for 291 yards and six touchdowns and averaged 7.5 yards per carry. Robinson had 21 carries for 83 yards and eight receptions for 90 yards in the Falcons' 20-13 loss at Pittsburgh as the focal point of an offense that had a limited passing game.


Stats and stuff
— The Panthers and Bears combined to score 96 points in Week 1, making it the highest-scoring season-opening game in NFL history. Unfortunately for the Panthers, they gave up 59 of those points, the most in franchise history.


— Panthers WR Jalen Coker had eight catches for a career-high 138 yards and two touchdowns in the Week 1 shootout with the Bears.


— RB Chuba Hubbard had a touchdown rushing and a touchdown receiving in Week 1 and remains the Panthers top option in the backfield.


— The Panthers defense allowed six touchdowns rushing against the Bears and two TDs in each quarter.


— Young is 4-1 against the Falcons, completing 110 of 165 pass attempts (66.7%) for 1,133 yards and seven touchdowns. He is 10-30 as a starter against the rest of the league.


— With Rush at quarterback, Drake London had only two catches for 29 yards and Kyle Pitts had no catches and only one target against Pittsburgh. London, Atlanta’s go-to wide receiver and Pitts, coming off a productive season at tight end, each received new contracts in the offseason.


— Tagovailoa did not participate in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Cornerback A.J. Terrell (shoulder) was a full participant on Thursday after being held out Wednesday. RG Chris Lindstrom (concussion protocol) was limited on Thursday after being held out Wednesday.


— The Falcons are 21-10 at home in the rivalry.


— The Falcons ranked 31st in passing yards and 30th in total yards following their weak offensive showing in their opener.

stories.headline: 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan named to USMNT squad, Christian Pulisic left out
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union phenom Cavan Sullivan, 16, headlines the 28-player roster named by U.S. men's national team manager Mauricio Pochettino for the upcoming FIFA international window.
stories.body:
Sixteen-year-old Philadelphia Union phenom Cavan Sullivan headlines the 28-player roster named by U.S. men's national team manager Mauricio Pochettino for the upcoming FIFA international window, while AC Milan attacker Christian Pulisic was left off the roster.

Overall, the team named by Pochettino sees the U.S. manager stay true to his word that the group would consist of a mix of young and veteran players. There are a total of 13 uncapped players named to the roster.

"It's a completely different approach than it was in the past," Pochettino said from New York during an online news conference. "The World Cup is in four years. We need to work with different objectives and goals."

In addition to Sullivan, the uncapped players include Crystal Palace attacker Zavier Gozo, Philadelphia Union defender Neil Pierre and New York Red Bulls forward Julian Hall.

There are also an equal number of veterans, with Bournemouth midfielder Tyler Adams and Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards also included in the squad.

The roster has five goal scorers from the World Cup earlier this summer, including Middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, Villarreal defender Alex Freeman, Strasbourg attacker Gio Reyna, Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Malik Tillman and Celtic defender Auston Trusty.

The USMNT will face Peru on Sept. 26 in Orlando, Chile three days later in St. Louis, followed by matches against Mexico on Oct. 3 in Glendale, Arizona, as well as Canada on Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minnesota. Players will begin reporting to Atlanta on Sept. 20.

ESPN was the first to report Sullivan's inclusion on the roster, and he figures to garner plenty of attention, having long been touted as a future star for the USMNT.

He signed a homegrown deal with the Philadelphia Union on May 9, 2024, at the age of 14, making him the fifth-youngest player to sign a first-team MLS contract. The deal contains a clause that allows him to be transferred to Manchester City when he turns 18 in 2027.

But it is Sullivan's recent form that has caught Pochettino's attention. Since the resumption of play following MLS' break due to the World Cup, Sullivan has scored six goals -- including goal contributions in each of his past seven league games -- and added eight assists.

In all competitions this season, Sullivan has nine goals and 15 assists, a staggering number for a 16-year-old.

"He deserved all the praise that he's getting I think because he's performing well, he's playing well, he's giving assists and scoring goals," Pochettino said. "He is special because he is 16 years old playing in this level in MLS."

If Sullivan -- who turns 17 on Sept. 28 -- makes his USMNT debut in any of the upcoming matches, he will be the second-youngest player to play for the U.S., behind only Freddy Adu. Adu first appeared for the USMNT at 16 years, 243 days when he came on as a substitute in a 0-0 draw against Canada on Jan. 22, 2006.

Pulisic's omission was somewhat expected. He has just recently returned to the Milan lineup after sustaining a bone bruise and microfracture in his lower leg during the USMNT's World Cup elimination at the hands of Belgium on July 6. He has been a substitute in both of his appearances for Milan this season.

It has been Pochettino's habit to only name players to the roster who have shown a consistent level of fitness over several weeks.

Pochettino didn't give a reason for why he didn't pick Pulisic.

"It's not a point that now the first camp of this new cycle I start to explain why it's one, why it is not another," Pochettino said.

Juventus' Weston McKennie and Real Salt Lake's Diego Luna were also ruled out due to injury. McKennie has yet to play for Juventus this season due to a muscle injury, while Luna is set to undergo arthroscopic surgery in the near future in order to address a lingering knee issue. He's expected to miss multiple months.

AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun was also left off the roster. He has yet to feature for Monaco since a proposed transfer to Everton fell through very late in the summer transfer window.

- Pulisic subs on as Milan humbled by Benfica in Europa League

- Luna, Musah and the USMNT's fringe players hoping for a bigger role in 2030

Pochettino did see fit to hand a recall to a pair of players who missed out on the 2026 World Cup. AC Milan midfielder Yunus Musah is back in the fold following some impressive performances for his club. He hasn't featured for the U.S. since the 2025 Concacaf Nations League finals 18 months ago.

West Bromwich Albion defender George Campbell returns for the first time since earning his sole U.S. cap against Venezuela in January 2025.

MIDFIELDERS (9): Tyler Adams (AFC Bournemouth/ENG; 58/2), Mathis Albert (Borussia Dortmund/GER; 0/0), Sebastian Berhalter (Middlesbrough/ENG; 18/2), Zavier Gozo (Crystal Palace/ENG; 0/0), Adri Mehmeti (Red Bull New York; 0/0), Yunus Musah (AC Milan/ITA; 47/1), Brooklyn Raines (New England Revolution; 0/0), Gio Reyna (RC Strasbourg Alsace/FRA; 43/10), Malik Tillman (Bayer Leverkusen/GER; 35/5)

stories.headline: GM: 'Door open' for star goalie Hellebuyck to remain with Jets
stories.summary: Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff didn't rule out the possibility that goaltender Connor Hellebuyck could remain with the team after going public with a trade demand. The Jets formally suspended Hellebuyck on Wednesday for failure to report to training camp.
stories.body:
Winnipeg Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff didn't rule out the possibility that star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck could remain with the team after going public with a trade demand.

The Jets formally suspended Hellebuyck on Wednesday for failure to report to training camp. The 33-year-old goaltender requested a trade during exit interviews after last season, his 11th with the franchise. Hellebuyck won the Hart Trophy as NHL MVP in 2025 and has won the Vezina Trophy as the NHL's top goaltender three times, being a finalist for the award five times.

"No doors are closed. He's a player that's under contract for five years. But at the end of the day, that's his choice," said Cheveldayoff at the opening of training camp on Thursday.

Cheveldayoff said there's no timeline for trading his star goaltender, something the Jets have been trying to do for "a long period of time," including during last June's NHL draft. While he pushed back on a report this week that categorized the offers for Hellebuyck as "terrible," the Jets GM said, "There's been nothing that's allowed us to say, 'OK, this works for both teams.'"

Hellebuyck and his agent made their trade demand public with a statement in late August, saying "I have tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options" in trading him.

"When Connor requested being traded, we kept it quiet. That was partly on his request as well. And we tried to make that work and we've been trying to make that work ever since," Cheveldayoff said.

There's been a wave of speculation about why Hellebuyck has asked out of Winnipeg just two seasons into a seven-year contract extension that he signed in Oct. 2023.

Cheveldayoff was asked about comments Hellebuyck made about the "blowback" his wife Andrea received after the goaltender led Team USA to Olympic gold in the 2026 Winter Olympics over Team Canada. Hellebuyck attended the State of the Union Address with all but five of his teammates, where President Donald Trump announced that the goalie would be awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

"What they endured, they shouldn't have had to," said Cheveldayoff of the social media abuse.

TSN reported this week that Hellebuyck will not waive his no-movement clause to join any of the six other Canadian NHL teams.

"I'm not going to get into the specific teams. My guess is to what his restrictions are in those regards. Again, the choices that he makes are the choices that he makes. I don't have an understanding as to why he made some of the choices that he made when talking about those kind of situations," Cheveldayoff said.

There's also been speculation about a "gentlemen's agreement" that might have been made between Cheveldayoff and Hellebuyck when the goalie re-signed in Winnipeg, that if he asked out during his contract, that request would be honored.

"A contract is a contract in the National Hockey League, period. There are no side agreements, there's no general agreements. The league doesn't allow for that. So I guess the fact is any notion around that would not have any merit," Cheveldayoff said.

The Jets GM was also asked if there was a "promise" made to Hellebuyck and Jets star center Mark Scheifele that the team would contend for the Stanley Cup annually when both players signed their extensions in Oct. 2023.

"Promise is an interesting word. We've been a team that's tried to be as competitive as we possibly can each and every year," he said.

But overall, the Jets GM wasn't looking to explore why Hellebuyck wanted out.

"I guess in my mind it's irrelevant. In my mind, I have to deal with the situation that's in front of me. Connor's made the choices and we'll just deal with him moving forward," he said.

The Jets GM addressed the challenge in trying to move Hellebuyck. Beyond finding a deal that helps Winnipeg stay competitive and Hellebuyck's trade protection, Cheveldayoff said it's a smaller market when trying to trade a No. 1 goalie vs. other positions.

"If you're a team that has a bona fide No. 1 goaltender and he's locked up and he's yours, you're probably not interested. And it's not disparaging Connor Hellebuyck or anything like that. It's just the goalie market in general," he said. "So the fact of the matter that a team might be on the list as an available option has a No. 1 goaltender, well, that's kind of a moot point."

Hellebuyck will begin losing salary if he's still suspended when the NHL regular season starts. His $8.5 million average annual value will not count against the Jets' salary cap.

stories.headline: Alexa Grasso shows off flyweight's elite status in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
It's uncommon for two fighters ranked in the pound-for-pound top 10 to meet in a bout with no championship at stake. But that was the case at Saturday's fourth annual Noche UFC, where Alexa Grasso faced Manon Fiorot.

Grasso is a former women's flyweight champion and Fiorot competed for the belt last year, so their status as MMA elites was well established before they fought. And when Grasso won by unanimous decision, she further solidified her standing in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

The top five of the rankings remains intact, and Grasso moves up from 10th to replace Fiorot at No. 6. Fiorot slips two positions to No. 8 in a pound-for-pound hierarchy in which seven of the 10 ranked women compete at flyweight (including Zhang Weili, the former UFC strawweight champion who last fought in an unsuccessful challenge of Valentina Shevchenko in November).

With Shevchenko injured and having vacated her title, there will be much scrambling for the top spot, which will be at stake when No. 5 Natalia Silva fights unranked Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 16. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

Other fighters receiving votes: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan.

stories.headline: Fantasy women's hoops: Finish the job and win the fantasy finals with these picks
stories.summary: The final edition of weekly picks take you from the WNBA's return to the end of the fantasy women's hoops finals.
stories.body:
The daily news and notes around the WNBA have actionable value when applied to fantasy women's basketball. From lineup changes to hot streaks to injury news, check this page regularly for updates from ESPN's fantasy analysts Eric Moody and André Snellings.

Resources: Rankings | Scoring leaders | Added/dropped | ESPN Fantasy app

Sept. 17: Four players to target in free agency

Andre Snellings: The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup has concluded, with Team USA staging a massive comeback in the championship game to bring home the gold. The tournament caused a break in the WNBA season right in the middle of the fantasy playoffs, but the break ends on Thursday when the season resumes... with the WNBA at an interesting junction.

All eight playoffs teams are already clinched, but there is plenty of room for teams to move up and down in the standings. In addition, teams will want to enter the postseason on a high note so they will need to play themselves back into form after the layoff. In addition, many of the player contracts signed after last offseason's Collective Bargaining Agreement were for a single year, so a large chunk of the league are effectively in contract years. So, even if a player's team may be out of the playoffs hunt, they may still have quite a bit to play for going into the offseason.

As always, we help you keep your team operating at its best by pointing out some players that may be available on your free agency wire that are performing well enough to be worthy of rostering or streaming.

Sydney Taylor, G, Chicago Sky (Rostered in 34.5% of ESPN Leagues): Taylor was one of the hotter scorers in the WNBA for most of the month of July, when she averaged 19.3 PPG during a 10-game stretch from July 7 through Aug. 1 before injuries slowed her down. She returned from a five-game absence for the end of August but was playing more limited minutes. The layoff gave her time to get healthier for the end of the season which could allow her to finish on another upswing.

Awa Fam, C, Seattle Storm (46.4%): With Ezi Magbegor (knee) out for the season, Fam may be asked to take a larger role for the Storm moving forward. The 20-year-old rookie has had some strong performances in her rookie season and has nightly double-double potential when getting near-starter minutes.

Awak Kuier, C, Dallas Wings (35.4%): Kuier has started six of the last seven games for the Wings with an expanded role since Azzi Fudd went down for the season. Kuier is one of the best shot-blockers and defenders in the league, averaging 3.3 BPG and 1.0 SPG along with a near double-double of 8.7 PPG and 7.4 RPG during that seven game stretch.

Lexi Held, G, Phoenix Mercury (1.4%): Held got a spot start in place of Kahleah Copper in the game before the break and turned in 11 points with three steals and three 3-pointers in 21 minutes. With both Kelsey Plum (leg) and Jovana Nogic (overseas commitment) out for the season, Held is likely to remain a starter for the remainder of the campaign and continue to be a solid source of scoring and 3-point shooting.

2026 fantasy women's basketball awards

Eric Moody: The 2026 season had everything fantasy managers could ask for, with stars delivering on expectations, breakout players and plenty of help from the waiver wire. With the fantasy season almost over, here are my awards for the players who made the biggest impact.

Fantasy MVP: A'ja Wilson, F/C, Las Vegas Aces

Wilson was the safest player in fantasy and once again delivered elite production across the board. She scored, rebounded, blocked shots and created steals at a level few players could match. Wilson ranks first in total fantasy points and fantasy points per game by a significant margin. If you drafted her at 1.01, she lived up to expectations.

Best scorer award for most fantasy points from points and 3-pointers: Kelsey Mitchell, G, Indiana Fever

Mitchell was one of the league's best sources of scoring and 3-pointers all season. She ranked third in 3-pointers per game while shooting 45.5% from beyond the arc, second in points per game and second in field goal attempts per game. Mitchell ranks fifth in total fantasy points largely because of that scoring production, making her a great return on her average draft position.

Box score award for most fantasy points from rebounds, assists, steals and blocks: Angel Reese, F/C, Atlanta Dream

Reese hasn't had to be a prolific scorer to help fantasy managers. Most of her value comes from everything else. She currently holds the single-season rebounding record, passing A'ja Wilson's mark of 451 from the 2024 season. Reese leads the league in rebounds per game and ranks third in steals per game. When you add in her points, assists and blocks, she ranks fourth in total fantasy points. Reese has generated more value from the non-scoring categories than any other player.

Matchup winner award for best fantasy week: A'ja Wilson, F/C, Las Vegas Aces

Wilson also delivered one of the best fantasy stretches of the season. From July 28 through Aug. 1, she scored 166 fantasy points across three games, including 28 points and 14 rebounds, 33 points with 10 rebounds and six assists, and 36 points with 12 rebounds. A week like that can swing an entire fantasy matchup.

Most underrated award for best player under 50% rostered: Leila Lacan, G, Connecticut Sun

Lacan was one of the better under-the-radar fantasy options this season for a Sun team that was one of the worst in the league. She averaged 23.1 fantasy points in 28.4 minutes per game, and her assists and steals gave her value even when the scoring wasn't there. Despite that production, Lacan remained available in far too many leagues for much of the season.
